newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ coalition talks enter fifth session.
newsitem.headline: NZ coalition talks enter fifth session.

text.p: Negotiating teams from the caretaker governing National party and New Zealand First went into their fifth round of talks on Tuesday.
New Zealand First was scheduled to meet the opposition Labour party team later on Tuesday.

Nationalist New Zealand First holds the balance of power after a general election on October 12 and is negotiating with both Labour and the conservative National party over the shape of the new government.

Going into the 2 p.m. talks, Prime Minister Jim Bolger threw his support behind the New Zealand horse Senator for today's Melbourne Cup, but would not be drawn on any matters relating to the negotiations.
He said a report Labour and New Zealand First had sought into the current round of state house rent rises was a matter for Housing Minister Murray McCully.
"I don't discuss the details of our talks. You know that. We have established that already." Bolger said.

Bolger's negotiating team included Deputy Prime Minister Don McKinnon, Attorney-General Paul East, Treaty Negotiations Minister Doug Graham, senior backbencher Max Bradford and the prime minister's chief of staff Rob Eaddy.

The New Zeakland First team included leader Winston Peters, deputy leader Tau Henare, employment spokesman Peter McCardle, party president Doug Woolerton, Peters' brother lawyer Wayne Peters and New Zealand First media officer Sarah Neems.
Peters declined to comment on the talks.
